3. In 1900, Margaret Abbot, a young American art student living in Paris decided to spend a Tuesday afternoon competing in a 9-hole tournament she saw advertised in the local paper. She showed up in her everyday street clothes—a heavy Victorian skirt and a fashionable hat—and finished the round with a respectable score of 47.Her prize for winning was a gilded porcelain bowl, which she kept as a pleasant souvenir of a "social outing." She eventually moved back to the States, lived a full life, and passed away in 1955. It wasn’t until decades after her death that an Olympic historian began digging through old French newspapers and discovered that the "social game" was actually an official part of the Paris Games. What was the unique, history-making achievement she accomplished without ever realizing it during her lifetime?
